citations.claim: Must declare as "Contains: Tree Nuts (Almonds)" — category designation required
citations.evidence: 21 U.S.C. 343(w)(2): for "a tree nut ... the term “name of the food source from which the major food allergen is derived” means the name of the specific type of nut" — "almonds" is exactly what is required; no "Tree Nuts" category designation.

citations.claim: Allergen declaration in plain language with category
citations.evidence: 101.4(h): "The common or usual name of ingredients of dietary supplements that are botanicals ... shall be consistent with the names standardized in Herbs of Commerce" — nothing on allergens. 343(w)(2) requires the specific nut, which "almonds" is.

citations.claim: "almonds (almonds)" redundant; "2 percent or less" improperly formatted; list sugar, salt in descending order
citations.evidence: 101.4(a)(2): the descending-order requirement does "not apply to ingredients present in amounts of 2 percent or less by weight when a listing of these ingredients is placed at the end of the ingredient statement following an appropriate quantifying statement, e.g., “Contains __ percent or less of ______”" — the label uses exactly this.

citations.claim: Must include "Manufactured by"/"Distributed by"/"Packed by"
citations.evidence: 101.5(a) is one sentence with no (a)(2): "The label of a food in packaged form shall specify conspicuously the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor." The qualifier is 101.5(c), and only "Where the food is not manufactured by the person whose name appears on the label".

citations.claim: Potassium labeling requirements
citations.evidence: 101.36(b)(2) has subparagraphs (i)-(iii) only; no (b)(2)(vi). And § 101.36 is "Nutrition labeling of dietary supplements".

otherClaims.claim: "Contains: almonds" lacks allergen category ("Tree Nuts (Almonds)") — not-real: 343(w)(2) requires "the name of the specific type of nut"

"almonds (almonds)" redundant/erroneous, list once — not-real: 343(w)(1)(B)(i) parenthetical "is not required when the common or usual name of the ingredient uses the name of the food source"; permitted, not a violation
"Contains 2 percent or less of sugar, salt" vague/non-compliant; list sugar, salt separately — not-real: 101.4(a)(2) permits "Contains __ percent or less of ______"
Qualifying phrase ("Manufactured by" etc.) always required — not-real: 101.5(c) requires it only "Where the food is not manufactured by the person whose name appears on the label"
Potassium 6% DV may be incorrect — not-real: 101.9(c)(8)(iii) 2% increments; (d)(8) gives "Potassium 235 mg 6%"

answers.notes: Control. Calls #1-#3 "definite compliance failures"; all three are not-real. Two non-existent paragraphs, one of them in the dietary-supplement section.

citations.claim: Potassium DV is 4,700 mg; 235 mg = 5%, label should read 5%
citations.evidence: 101.9(c)(9) is the DRV table for food components (fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, total carbohydrate, sodium, dietary fiber, protein, added sugars) — no potassium; the 4,700 mg potassium RDI is in (c)(8)(iv). And (c)(8)(iii): vitamin/mineral percentages "shall be expressed to the nearest 2-percent increment up to and including the 10-percent level", so 5% is not a permitted value; 101.9(d)(8) itself gives "Potassium 235 mg 6%".

citations.claim: Indented under Total Sugars, worded "Includes 0g Added Sugars"
citations.evidence: 101.9(c)(6)(iii): "Added sugars content shall be indented under Total Sugars and shall be prefaced with the word “Includes” followed by the amount (in grams) “Added Sugars”". Label prints "Added Sugars 0g".

citations.claim: Footnote must include "(DV)"
citations.evidence: 101.9(d)(9): "The footnote shall state: “*The % Daily Value tells you how much a nutrient in a serving of food contributes to a daily diet. 2,000 calories a day is used for general nutrition advice.”" — no "(DV)"; the label prints exactly this.

citations.claim: Must be rounded and prefaced with "about" when not a whole number → "about 9"
citations.evidence: 101.9(b)(8)(i): rounding to the nearest whole number is "shall", but "Rounding should be indicated by the use of the term about" — "about" is a should, stated by the answer as must.

citations.claim: Parenthetical repeating the name is erroneous; use "almonds"
citations.evidence: § 101.4 has no rule against a parenthetical repeating the ingredient name. 21 U.S.C. 343(w)(1)(B)(i): the parenthetical food source "is not required when the common or usual name of the ingredient uses the name of the food source" — not required, not prohibited; redundant, not a violation.

citations.ref: FD&C Act §403(w), FALCPA (as amended by FASTER Act)
citations.claim: "Contains: almonds" satisfies the allergen rule
citations.evidence: 21 U.S.C. 343(w)(1)(A): "the word “Contains”, followed by the name of the food source ... is printed immediately after or is adjacent to the list of ingredients (in a type size no smaller than the type size used in the list of ingredients)".

citations.claim: Sodium 0 only if < 5 mg
citations.evidence: 101.9(c)(4): sodium "expressed as zero when the serving contains less than 5 milligrams of sodium".

citations.claim: Added sugars 0 only if < 0.5 g
citations.evidence: 101.9(c)(6)(iii): added sugars "if the serving contains less than 0.5 gram, the content may be expressed as zero".

citations.claim: Fortificants must appear in the ingredient list
citations.evidence: 101.4(a)(1): ingredients "shall be listed by common or usual name in descending order of predominance by weight" — added fortificants are ingredients.

citations.claim: Fortification must be consistent with 104.20
citations.evidence: 21 CFR 104.20 (eCFR, fetched 2026-10-09) is a fortification policy: (a) "a uniform set of principles that will serve as a model"; "manufacturers who elect to fortify foods are urged to utilize these principles"; nutrients "may appropriately be added". Not a binding requirement to "comply" with.

citations.evidence: 101.12(b) Table 2 holds the RACCs; RTE cereal 43 g or more per cup is 60 g (the answer's "if it is 55 g" is hypothetical).
